## Task

> `node2` runs an HTTP service on TCP port 8080, reachable over the private
> network shared with `node1` and `node3`. Make `node1` answer DNS for that
> network so `node3` can reach the service by the name `app.internal` without
> any local hosts-file entry.

## Trial `dns-hostname-override-alpine__LJzcSYZ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly configured node1's dnsmasq to resolve app.internal to node2's IP and pointed node3's resolver at node1 without touching /etc/hosts, and directly verified end-to-end HTTP reachability by name both before and after rebooting all three nodes. It also discovered and fixed a real gap (node2's HTTP service was not actually running) as a necessary prerequisite. The mandatory restart protocol was completed for all three nodes with baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state, though the fixed after-executor snapshot could not independently confirm node1's new boot identity via SSH at capture time (a minor evidence gap, not a functional failure, since the executor's own probes show the transition).

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.900 | 30/3 (+8 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 (dnsmasq) resolves the name app.internal to node2's private IP address
  - **Why:** UCI dhcp address record '/app.internal/10.100.101.11' added and committed on node1, dnsmasq restarted and confirmed bound on 10.100.101.10:53. node3's nslookup against node1 returns the correct address, and this was re-verified identically after node1's reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f6966cccde824ab6`, `cmd-1a1167241f644fc5`, `cmd-e453a20c3c3142ac`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node3 uses node1 as its DNS resolver (so app.internal resolves) without any local /etc/hosts entry
  - **Why:** node3's /etc/dhcpcd.conf was updated with a static domain_name_servers override pointing at node1 (10.100.101.10), dhcpcd restarted, and resolv.conf confirmed updated. /etc/hosts on node3 was checked and shown to contain no app.internal entry, both before and after node3's reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-6d44c8a2f0bb4776`, `cmd-ec4674cb0cc648a9`, `cmd-4c8b335e373045d3`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** node3 can reach node2's HTTP service on port 8080 by the name app.internal
  - **Why:** End-to-end curl from node3 to http://app.internal:8080/ succeeded, returning content served by node2, both immediately after configuration and after all three nodes were individually rebooted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-30599638dd6a4d39`, `cmd-ab35b6c9b17a4a74`, `cmd-4c8b335e373045d3`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** node2 actually runs the HTTP service on port 8080 (implicit precondition stated as fact in the task)
  - **Why:** Initial discovery showed nothing listening on 8080 on node2 (curl failed, empty proc/net/tcp). Executor installed python3 and created a persistent OpenRC service 'app-http' serving on 0.0.0.0:8080, enabled at boot, and verified listening via curl and the final listening-sockets snapshot. This is a reasonable prerequisite fix rather than scope creep, since the task's contract requires the service to be reachable.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-89fb6988c5b748ba`, `cmd-8217a81ebe864406`, `cmd-14a83312ba8345d4`
- **req-5 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
  - **Why:** For each node, a pre-restart boot_id/uptime/service baseline was captured, a reboot was issued (with an initial failed attempt on node1 due to a missing nohup binary, corrected via a background subshell), and post-restart a differing boot_id plus healthy state (dnsmasq/UCI on node1, app-http service on node2, resolver/hosts/curl on node3) was directly observed. The fixed after_executor snapshot independently confirms new boot_ids for node2 and node3; for node1 the fixed snapshot's SSH-based boot-identity probe failed to connect at capture time, so that particular cross-check is unconfirmed, though the executor's own in-session probes directly show the boot_id change and recovery.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-01537b3513e34213`, `cmd-9b28a5f98d5e45be`, `cmd-922b6fa62d9f40fb`, `cmd-e453a20c3c3142ac`, `cmd-2f050f5136c94bc6`, `cmd-f2c08ed5636a4e2c`, `cmd-e91a885d0496433b`, `cmd-363725f04429497f`, `cmd-c9d13dbd7149462c`, `cmd-7d8343aa25684a8e`, `cmd-7e87339a88664c8b`, `cmd-4c8b335e373045d3`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. All state-changing executor commands map clearly to satisfying the task contract or the mandated restart protocol: UCI DNS record on node1, dhcpcd resolver override on node3, python3 install and app-http OpenRC service on node2 (a legitimate fix for the stated-but-absent HTTP service), and three individually acknowledged reboots. No unnecessary or abandoned mutations were found; the one failed reboot attempt on node1 (nohup missing) was a corrective retry rather than an unrelated experiment, and left no residue. Package-health diffs and a new /tmp/state/dnsmasqsec entry on node1, plus /tmp/reboot.log on node2/node3, are expected side effects of the dnsmasq restart and reboot cycle rather than executor-caused residue requiring cleanup.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-9b28a5f98d5e45be`, `cmd-96b4443c7b0b4520`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`
